Due to the solubility of CO in water at ambient 2 pressures, this portion is amenable to analysis via Henry’s law as the mole fraction of CO in the aqueous membrane will generally be quite small (< 0.03). CV-2 2 corresponds to the interior of the membrane and is where simultaneous diffusion and reaction of the species of interest occur. This section was described with the 19 appropriate form of the reaction-diffusion equation in which each species diffuses in the z-direction (through the membrane) while simultaneously reacting. CA is known to demonstrate Michaelis-Menten kinetics, and the modeling work was conducted using literature data for an enzyme with pH optimum of 8.5. CV-3 represents the water sweep stream where convection mass transfer carries the bicarbonate/CO 2 away from the membrane surface. This section can be modeled with the convection- diffusion equation where each species diffuses in the z-direction (into the sweep stream) and advects in the x-direction (along the membrane surface). Equations representing the reaction and mass transfer phenomena in each region were solved numerically for a system at 25 °C.
